full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed. J:- The Plaintiffs have preferred this revisional application under section 115 (4) against the order of the District Judge, Dhaka and sought for Leave to revision and this court granted leave and issued rule calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 24.10.2007 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 170 of 2007 allowing the same by setting aside the order dated 13.2.2007 passed by the learned Assistant Judge Nowabgonj Adalat, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 239 of 2005 rejecting the application for better statement filed by the defendant opposite party and the learned district Judge further ordered allowing the petition dated 10.4.2003 filed by the defendant for amendment of written statement which is not the subject of the Civil Revision No. 170 of 2007 should not be set aside or such order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The fact necessary for the disposal of the rule is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 26 of 2001 in the court of Assistant Judge Karanigonj Adalat, Dhaka for permanent and mandatory injunction in respect of 21 decimals of land of C.S. and S.A. plot No. 37 of Mouja Joynagar under P.S. Karanigonj, District Dhaka praying that a decree for permanent injunction be passed against the defendant restraining the defendant from entering in to the 'ka' schedule property and from making any construction and interfering with the possession of the plaintiffs in respect of 'ka' schedule property and also prayed for decree for mandatory injunction from demolishing the illegal construction of the defendant in respect of "kha" schedule property of the plaint. 

 4. The defendant filed written statement and after the filling the Advocate Commissioner report the defendant filed an application on 10.4.2003 before the trial court under order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of written statement in respect of 9 decimals of land of C.S. and S.A. Plot No. 36 and the learned Assistant Judge after hearing both the parties rejected the amendment petition on 10.5.2003. There after the defendant filed Civil Revision No. 18 of 2004 before the District Judge under section 115 (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure Code against the order of Assistant Judge and the said Civil Revision was disallowed finally on 18.3.2004 as the revision case was out of time by 190 days against which the defendant preferred Civil Revisional application under section 115 (4) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The rule was issued and ultimately after hearing the rule by learned Judge of a single Bench of this court was pleased to discharge the rule by judgment and order dated 4.4.2005. 

 5. The defendant, thereafter, filed an application with better statement on 31.1.2007 and after hearing the parties the learned Assistant Judge rejected the better statement on 13.2.2007 against which the defendant filed Civil Revision No. 170 of 2007 before the District Judge, Dhaka on 7.6.2007 under section 115 (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure which was filed out of time by 113 days. The learned District Judge heard the Civil Revision on 17.10.2007 and fixed 24.10.2007 for judgment. The learned District Judge heard the Civil Revision and was pleased to allow the Civil Revision and set aside the order dated 13.2.2007 passed by the Trial court by judgment and order dated 24.10.2007 and also allowed the amendment petition dated 10.4.2003. 

 6. The plaintiff-petitioners then being aggrieved by the aforesaid order passed by the District Judge, Dhaka preferred the present Civil Revision before this court under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil procedure and learned Single Judge of the High Court Division granted leave and also issued rule as stated above. 

 7. Mr. Moin Uddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has placed the annexures-A to K (1) Order of Trial Court and also placed the impugned order dated 24.10.2007 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka and submitted that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal and that the learned District Judge has passed order beyond scope of the subject matter of the civil revision case No. 170 of 2007 in as much as the defendant preferred Civil Revision before the learned District Judge against the order dated 13.2.2007 passed by the Assistant Judge but the learned District Judge while disposing the revisional application has considered certain orders which were not impugned before the revisional Court and arrived at erroneous findings and allowed the amendment of the written statement though such question was resolved and closed by judgment and order dated 4.4.2005 in the civil Revision No. 2127 of 2004 and committed fundamental error of law and thereby an important question of law has arisen which calls for interference by this Hon'ble Court. Mr. Moinuddin further submits that the impugned order suffers from gross illegality as the learned District Judge has acted in access of his jurisdiction and those being the important question of law has caused failure of justice. 

 8. Mr. Moshfequddin Bakhtear, the learned Advocate for the opposite party appearing before this Court has taken me though the impugned order and pointed out that the learned District Judge has committed no error in allowing the revisional and infect the learned District Judge allowed the better statement having regard to the provision of Order 6 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure and hence no interference is called for by this Hon'ble Court. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned District Judge upon elaborate discussions of both facts and law allowed the revisional application and has committed no error of law and no important question of law has arisen which needs be resolved by this court and thereby the rule is liable to be discharged. Order 6 rule 5 runs thus: "R.S. Further and better statement or particulars. A further and better statement of the nature of the claim or defence, or further and better particulars of any matter stated in, any pleading; may in all cases be ordered, upon such terms, as to costs and otherwise, as may be just" 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and I also perused the annexures and the impugned order. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge has rejected the better statement on the finding in as much as বিবাদী পক্ষে দাখিলী better statement এর তফসিল দৃষ্টে তাহা নালিশী সম্পত্তি নহে এমতাবস্থায় উক্ত  statement অপ্রয়োজনীয় বিবেচনায় না মঞ্জুর করা হইল।" 

 I have also perused the application for making better statement. (Annexure — H) where, in the body of the application it has been stated 

 "বর্তমানে বিবাদী তফশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে ৭ (সাত) শতাংশ ভূমির ভোগ দখলে আছেন। বাকী ২ (দদুই) শতাংশ জায়গা ৩৫নং দাগে ৩৭ রহিয়াছে and also given particulars of the land in the schedule জেলা-ঢাকা, থানা ও সাব রেজিষ্ট্র অফিস কেরানীগঞ্জ অধীনে রায়তি জোত স্বাত্বের ভিটি বাড়ীর পরিচয় ঢাকা কালেক্টরীর ৭৮৪৯ নং তৌজর ৩৯২ নং জয়নগর মৌজার সি,এস ১৭৩ নং খতিয়ানের সি,এস ৩৬(ছত্রিশ) নং দাগের বাড়ী ০৯ শতাংশ যাহার এস, এ খতিয়ান নং-১৬৭ এস এ দাগ নং-৩৬ নামজারী খতিয়ান নং-১৬৭/২ দাগ নং ৩৬ আর এস খতিয়ান নং-২৯৫ আর এস দাগ নং-১২২ জমির পরিমাণ ৭ ২/১ শতাংশ ওয়ারিশান শুত্রে ২ ২/১ শতাংশ একুনে ৮৯ শতাংশযাহার চৌহদ্দি উত্তরে আবুল কাসেম দক্ষিনে জিলা বোর্ডের সড়ক পূর্বে আবদুল মান্নান ও হাজী আশ্রাফ আলী পাশ্চিমে শোহরাব আলী গং-। " Where from it appears that the learned Advocate for the defendant mentioned only Plot No. 36 and as such the findings of the trial court appear to have been made on the basis of the records and noted correctly that the Plot No. 36 does not attract as the suit is relating to plot No. 37. The learned District Judge in the impugned order quoted the order of the learned Assistant Judge, then considered the application for amendment dated 10.4.2003, and finally considered the order dated 13.2.2007 regarding better statement passed by the learned Assistant Judge and recorded findings as to better statement:-"The better statement should help the court in order to determine the real question of controversy between the parties with the proceedings. The learned Lower court has failed to appreciate the provisions of law and arrived at wrong decision occasioning failure of justice- and allowed the revision. The operating portion of the order runs as follows:- 

 that this Civil Revision is allowed on contest. The impugned order is hereby set as r1111 aside. It is further ordered that the amendment petition dated 10.4.2003 filed by the petitioner is allowed. Amend the written statement and register accordingly." 

 10. From the quoted order it reveals that the learned Judge also allowed an application for amendment dated 10.04.2003 filed by the defendant which was not the subject matter of the revision and from the order it clearly indicates that the learned District Judge exercised the jurisdiction beyond the scope of subject matter which is not expected from a Senior Judicial Officer like District Judge, Dhaka and it further reveals from the impugned order that the learned District Judge has not reversed the findings of the Trial court in as much as the Trial court recorded clear findings that the statement made in application for better statement does not relate to the suit property and in such circumstances, I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and therefore, I consider that an important question of law has been raised before this court and in the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of my discussion the impugned order is not sustainable in law.
